data.title: Saudi Steel Pipes' (TADAWUL:1320) Conservative Accounting Might Explain Soft Earnings

Zooming In On Saudi Steel Pipes' Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

For the year to September 2026, Saudi Steel Pipes had an accrual ratio of -0.27. That indicates that its free cash flow quite significantly exceeded its statutory profit. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of ر.س473m, well over the ر.س153.1m it reported in profit. Saudi Steel Pipes shareholders are no doubt pleased that free cash flow improved over the last twelve months.

data.title: Centrus Energy Fell 70%, But The Story Isn't Over
data.description:

Holding Centrus Energy from the start of the year would have meant a 70.1% loss, including dividends. The Two Centrus Energy Stories Investors Had To Weigh

The shares cost US$243 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Centrus Energy then had to choose between two very different futures.

On the upbeat side, one narrative saw a fair value of US$304, a price implied by assumptions about strong HALEU demand, with Centrus as the only proven US supplier that was expected to gain market share and premium pricing as Russian enrichment capacity receded.

The cautious view pointed to a fair value of US$106, a level tied to concerns that dependence on a few government and utility contracts and shifting energy policies could create sharp revenue swings and much thinner profit margins over time.

What The Evidence Did To The Centrus Energy Argument

The $900 million Department of Energy HALEU contract, a backlog that reached US$5.4b, and multi year fuel deals with Oklo, X energy, Antares and Radiant all leaned toward the bullish Centrus Energy story built on contracted demand. At the same time, revenue in Q3 2026 was US$55.5 million compared with US$74.9 million a year earlier, even as net margin climbed from 5.2% to 56.9%. Taken together, the period cut both ways.

The big swing factor was not sentiment but how far contract wins and margin shifts actually backed the earlier profitability claim. For another stock with a grand narrative, you would want to track the mix of backlog, reported revenue and net margin each quarter and see whether locked in orders are turning into stable sales and durable profitability.

What Centrus Energy's Price Drop Now Asks You To Believe

Centrus Energy trades at US$81.43, a long way from where it started the year, and this Narrative's Fair Value now sits above that level according to CentryResearch, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote the Narrative.

The core pitch is that HALEU enrichment remains a scarce fuel chokepoint rather than just another uranium product. For the fall to look like an opportunity rather than a warning, a buyer today would need to believe domestic HALEU demand and supportive policy endure long enough for Centrus Energy to run meaningful commercial volumes.

"Among publicly traded companies, Centrus Energy is one of the most directly positioned to benefit from growing demand for HALEU. Centrus has decades of experience in uranium enrichment and is currently one of the few U.S.-based companies pursuing domestic HALEU production."

From Centrus Energy To Critical Metals

Centrus Energy puts fuel at the center of your thesis. One step away, reactors and grids also need reliable high performance materials.

Modern turbines, vehicles and defense hardware rely on powerful permanent magnets. Those parts only work because rare earth elements give them strength and efficiency.

Another business focuses on mining those elements and turning them into magnet materials. It runs extraction and processing so customers can source magnets closer to home.

As clean energy and advanced manufacturing lean on these components, the role of that supplier may keep evolving in important ways.

Examining Cashflow Against Internity's Earnings

As finance nerds would already know, the accrual ratio from cashflow is a key measure for assessing how well a company's free cash flow (FCF) matches its profit. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. Zooming In On AF Gruppen's Earnings

As finance nerds would already know, the accrual ratio from cashflow is a key measure for assessing how well a company's free cash flow (FCF) matches its profit. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, AF Gruppen recorded an accrual ratio of -0.49. Therefore, its statutory earnings were very significantly less than its free cashflow. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of kr2.4b, well over the kr1.34b it reported in profit. AF Gruppen's free cash flow actually declined over the last year, which is disappointing, like non-biodegradable balloons. Having said that, there is more to the story. We can see that unusual items have impacted its statutory profit, and therefore the accrual ratio.

How Do Unusual Items Influence Profit?

While the accrual ratio might bode well, we also note that AF Gruppen's profit was boosted by unusual items worth kr181m in the last twelve months. While it's always nice to have higher profit, a large contribution from unusual items sometimes dampens our enthusiasm. We ran the numbers on most publicly listed companies worldwide, and it's very common for unusual items to be once-off in nature. And that's as you'd expect, given these boosts are described as 'unusual'. Assuming those unusual items don't show up again in the current year, we'd thus expect profit to be weaker next year (in the absence of business growth, that is).

Our Take On AF Gruppen's Profit Performance

AF Gruppen's profits got a boost from unusual items, which indicates they might not be sustained and yet its accrual ratio still indicated solid cash conversion, which is promising. Considering all the aforementioned, we'd venture that AF Gruppen's profit result is a pretty good guide to its true profitability, albeit a bit on the conservative side.
